en.title: Minimum Load Difference Between Two Servers
en.description:
Assign each process to exactly one of two servers; a server's load is the sum of the integer loads assigned to it. Output the minimum absolute difference between the two total loads; one server may have no processes.

The input/output and examples are compiled by CSWork; numeric ranges marked as this site's are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: This site's standard input: the first line contains n (1..2000); the second line contains n integer loads, and the sum of the absolute values of all loads does not exceed 200000.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: the loads can be split into 7 and 8, a difference of 1; the total 15 is odd, so a difference of 0 is impossible. Example 2: the only split is 7 and 0, a difference of 7. Example 3: the total of all items is 0, so one server takes everything and the other stays empty, a difference of 0.
hints: Record the reachable subset sums in an integer bitset; when a load is negative, shift the lower bound of the represented range accordingly. Finally, find the largest reachable sum that does not exceed half of the total.
